rows.label: ascension picture: fighter fields
rows.why: The picture's own state on the fighter (fade, ages, the tallies as last seen, the threads); written by tickAscend only, read by the draws only.

rows.label: ascension picture: the presentation call
rows.why: tickAscend runs on the presentation clock, which runs through hit stops and after the match; so the picture plays through the freeze and closes itself at `over`.

rows.label: ascension picture: tickAscend
rows.why: Drives the window's picture off ultRise && !over && alive (Canopy's rule), finds each shaft blow by `hits` rising while lit and each heal by riseTally.bless rising; writes presentation fields, tags and taught only.

rows.label: ascension picture: the world call (under both balls)
rows.why: World pass under both balls: the rise column, the halo, the foot pools (bloom share 0).

rows.label: ascension picture: the emissive call (over both fighters)
rows.why: The shafts' 3-unit cores under `lighter` (v74: 'under lighter ONLY the core'), both shells cut out.

rows.label: ascension picture: the shafts' hook in drawWeapon
rows.anchor: if ((f.treeFade > 0 || f.ultTree) && this.drawTreeWeapon(m, f, reach, dim)) return;
rows.code:
/* ASCENSION'S SHAFTS (v74 section 6.1): while the shafts are lit and
       while they shorten, the blades are drawn at their REST length and the
       light runs on from them to the edge of the live hall
       (`drawAscendWeapon`) -- `reachMul` is 10 and would draw the blade art
       ~680 units long, past every wall, and it stays 10 through the verdict
       when the match ends in the window. `ascendFade` is 0 and `ultRise` null
       on every other relic, so this is two comparisons on fields nothing
       else writes. */
    if ((f.ascendFade > 0 || f.ultRise) && this.drawAscendWeapon(m, f, dim)) return;
rows.why: While lit, closing, or through a verdict that left the window open, the blades are drawn at rest and the light runs on to the live hall's edge; reachMul 10 would draw the blade art ~680 units long past every wall.

rows.label: ascension picture: the body trail's ghost
rows.code:
/* ASCENSION (v74 section 6.1): the body trail is fed by `move`, which a
       pinned ball skips, and `tickRise` carries the ball away from it -- so
       for the whole window the trail sat where the cast was, a ghost of the
       ball on the floor it left. Not drawn while the picture is up; `move`
       refills it within 0.15s of the release, inside the close.
       `ascendFade` is 0 on every other relic. */
    const tr = f.ascendFade > 0 ? [] : f.trail;
rows.why: drawFighter's body trail is fed by move(), which a pinned ball skips; tickRise carries the ball away, so the stale trail drew a ghost ball at the cast point for the whole window. Hidden while ascendFade > 0 (0 on every other relic).

rows.label: ascension picture: the drawing methods
rows.why: drawAscend (column, halo, pools), _ascendEdge/_ascendLen (the live hall's edge), drawAscendWeapon (bodies, motes, the blades at rest), drawAscendTop (cores, then the threads over them).

fx_spec: NONE. Both fx.js copies are left as they are. The design's field ("light motes drifting down the shafts, both copies") is drawn in the world pass instead: 8 motes a shaft, drifting at 90 u/s just outside the shaft body, positioned by shellHash and the clock (no rng). Measured reason (an_fxprobe.py, on the base link, 133 Ascension windows, 16 foes x 2 seeds, both sides): the single m.ultFx slot has no `life` entry for Angelus, so it gets the default. Angelus holds it for a median 0.633 s of window clock (max 0.717), which is 7.4% of the window and 4.36% of the lit time; the shafts only light at window clock 0.35. The slot is lost to the opponent's cast in 21 of 133 windows, expires in 109 and ends with the match in 3. A SPECS field fires once, at the cast position, and that position is a median 226 units (p10 79, p90 383) from the hang point the shafts turn about. A slot-borne field would be gone before the shafts light, would sit on the floor the ball has left, and could not follow two turning shafts. This is the same finding as the Zenith (v98) and Canopy (v99) precedents.

HOW EACH PART OF v74 6.1 WAS READ
1. Canopy's rule. The picture reads `ultRise && !over && alive` and keeps its own state on the fighter (ascendFade, ascendAge, ascendLit, ascendOut, ascendSeen, ascendHeal, ascendFx), driven by tickAscend in tickPresentation. The sim reads none of it; the only other writes are m.tags and m.taught (the tag rule). It never uses m.ultFx.
2. The rise. A column from the ball to the floor comes up over 0.05 s and fades over 0.4 s after the arrival. The halo is source-over at r 1.1R in the school's glow (not lighter), comes up over the 0.35 s rise and goes with the close.
3. The shafts.
   - The blades are drawn at REST length. Each shaft's light runs from the shell to whichever is nearer, the end of the hit segment or the edge of the live hall (inset-aware and clipped), so nothing is drawn past a wall.
   - The body is a soft bar 10 u wide at half max (half-width 7) at 0.55, source-over, with a warm #FFD98A edge so it reads as light and not as a white rod.
   - The 3 u core is the only part under lighter, with both shells cut out.
   - An ignition flare runs for 0.12 s at the arrival.
   - Each shaft's foot has a pool where it meets the hall.
   - bladeSegments and the hit geometry are untouched.
4. A shaft hit.
   - The blade's own flash is the engine's.
   - A gold thread with a dark-rimmed bead runs from the blow's contact point (the `hit` beat resolveHit filed that step) up the nearest shaft to the ball over 0.25 s, drawn over the cores. It starts at the shade on a shade hit (reading 11).
   - When riseTally.bless rises (the next live step), the halo flares gold for 0.3 s and BLESSING n goes up on the caster. One tag at a time; the first one teaches.
5. The close. The shafts shorten to blades over 0.3 s and dim to 0.35. The halo goes. The ball's drop and landing are the engine's.
   - At `over` it is the same close on the presentation clock, with the blades drawn at rest while reachMul stays 10.
   - I did NOT draw a presentation-only "ball drop" after the kill. The ball stays where the frozen sim holds it, like every relic's ball at the verdict. Rick's to overrule.
   - A dead caster is drawn by drawShatter (no weapon), so its halo and shafts go with the ball.
6. Added fix: the body trail's ghost. move() feeds the trail and a pinned ball skips move(), so the stale trail drew a ghost ball at the cast point for the whole window. It is hidden while ascendFade > 0 (a replace row on `const tr = f.trail;`, an anchor no other builder uses).
7. The silhouette is `_tbRadiant`, unchanged: it reads 2nd of 7 twinblades.
8. The hexagon needs nothing: pinFree is 1, as the build doc says.

FINDING FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR (not a picture defect)
- litWeapon draws every lit weapon through ONE module-level scratch canvas, `_litScratch`. It grows to the largest weapon ever drawn, never shrinks, and is cleared whole on every call.
- The base link's x10 placeholder grows it to 1463-1597 px, against 815-863 px on an-final. From then on every lit weapon in that page pays for it:
  - Spellbreaker's drawWeapon runs 290-640 ms on the base against 90-147 ms on an-final (headless);
  - the cost carries into the NEXT match in the same page (Spellbreaker v Dawnbringer after an Angelus fight: 288-636 ms).
- So cost.py and cost2.py, which interleave both arms in one page, charged the OFF arm's bloated scratch to the ON arm as well: spellbreaker ~400 ms and rise/close 13-19 ms a call in both arms. cost3.py (one process per arm) is the clean reading.
- The rows remove the problem for Angelus, but any future relic that draws a very long lit weapon will hit the same scratch. Worth an item.
